title: What is the Eagles’ offensive identity? Not ‘good enough,’ says Nick Sirianni after loss to Rams | The Early Bird
description: Eagles fans flocked to the exits as Jalen Hurts commanded the huddle on the Eagles’ final drive. The offense faced third-and-17 with the game on the line, but the result...
fullText:
Eagles fans flocked to the exits as Jalen Hurts commanded the huddle on the Eagles' final drive.

The offense faced third-and-17 with the game on the line, but the result felt like a foregone conclusion.

The Eagles lost, 24-20, to the Los Angeles Rams and fell to 2-2. The offense turned in a listless second half, the defense capitulated two back-breaking drives late, and somehow this team erased a 10-point lead built up mostly off turnovers and some opportune moments from reserve wide receiver Darius Cooper in the end zone.

Afterward, Hurts summed the afternoon up with two words, over and over.

The Eagles finishing 0-for-12 on third down in the game, the worst ratio from any Eagles game since 1991?

What about the Eagles once-again stagnant offense in third quarter? The offense has managed just three first downs in the third quarter across all four of the games they've played this season, the worst tally in the NFL by a wide margin. The group has just 12 second-half first downs, which is also the worst total in the league.

Hurts finished the game 12-for-27 for just 93 passing yards and two touchdowns set up by takeaways on defense. Beside two games that he left due to injury, Sunday was the lowest yardage tally Hurts has recorded since becoming the Eagles starting quarterback in 2021.

This is as good a time as any to contextualize the offensive performance. The group came into the game without DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, or Lane Johnson. Johnson was a late addition to the inactives list for personal reasons. Saquon Barkley left in the first quarter with a hamstring injury and did not return as well.

Players did not know Johnson would be unavailable until they reported to the stadium the morning of the game, Eagles left tackle Jordan Mailata said. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni did not offer any details about Johnson's absence, either. Missing the 36-year-old gave way to the Eagles starting third-round rookie Markel Bell at right tackle without another healthy tackle on the active roster. It also left them with just seven offensive linemen available to dress, meaning the team was one player short of the permitted 48 on the active roster because that number requires at least eight offensive linemen to be included.

"I've got to figure it out," Hurts said when asked about the injuries. "However it looks, whatever it means. Find a way to win the game."

Most importantly, the late switch left the Eagles offense seemingly even less prepared for the pressure wrinkles from the Rams. According to Next Gen Stats, Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula sent extra rushers at Hurts on 18 of his dropbacks (60.6%), with Hurts going 5-for-16 on those plays. And on the Eagles' 12 third downs, the Rams blitzed on all but one.

When asked about those issues, Hurts defaulted back to the line of the day.

"Poor execution," Hurts said. "I don't think there's any other way to put it."

The optimist's view of the Eagles' second-half collapse will likely point to the absence of quite possibly the four most important offensive contributors not named Jalen Hurts for most of the game. The team entered Sunday as underdogs and perhaps wouldn't have been viewed as harshly if not for a somewhat overachieving first-half performance relative to what most expected the game to look like because of the injury report.

Still, facing third-and-goal from the two-yard line with a 10-point lead and 8 minutes remaining, the Eagles somehow managed to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory largely due to an offense devoid of an identity.

"Right now, it hasn't been good enough," Sirianni said. "I think that's still. You're trying to make sure as you find out who you are that you're playing with detail and you're playing with together and you're playing with toughness. We've still got ways to go there. It's obvious that we're still trying to figure that out."

The detail, in particular, has been lacking. A botched play came on the pivotal third-and-goal, courtesy of Cam Jurgens pulling across the formation and interfering with Hurts trying to secure the snap and hand the bal off to Tank Bigsby. And facing fourth-and-goal from the 2, Sirianni elected to keep the offense on the field for an incomplete pass to Cooper.

Sirianni was (understandably) aggressive trying to make it a three-possession game, but the decision backfired. The Rams drove 98 yards for a touchdown and got the ball back quickly after the Eagles offense turned in its 19th three-and-out of the season (second highest in the NFL.)

"I'm trying to make it a three-score game," Sirianni said. "We would have went up 13, but I wanted to make it a three-score game right there. Fourth-and-2 from the 2, you leave them in a true backed-up scenario. I'm very well aware of how fourth-down decisions go as the head coach. You go for it and you get it, great. You go for it and you don't get it, that's on the head coach. And we didn't get it, so that's on me."

An optimist's view would also point to the fact that the Eagles have been here before with Hurts under center and Sirianni at the helm. You might remember the team also got off to a 2-2 start in 2024. The offensive line implored Sirianni to pivot toward more of a run-first approach, Sirianni shaved his head, and the Eagles went on a magical run to Super Bowl LIX and left Caesars Superdome with the organization's second Lombardi Trophy.

That page doesn't seem to be in Sean Mannion's 2026 playbook, though. The Eagles ranked fifth in EPA/rush through the first four games of 2024. This season, they're 24th. They've had moving pieces along the offensive line in three of the first four games and Barkley has now suffered a stinger and a hamstring injury already this season. Backup running back Tank Bigsby also suffered an apparent injury late in the fourth quarter.

What is apparent is that the Eagles now have an urgency to figure out what this year's about face is going to look like. A training camp spent harping on under-center formations and play-action passing concepts hasn't kept them from ranking in the bottom five in the NFL in terms of usage in both categories.

Less than a week removed from challenging his teammates to ask themselves "who are we?" in the wake of the loss to the Bears, Hurts didn't have much of an answer himself to explain the second defeat in a six-day span.

"You're finding your flow," Hurts said. "I think collectively as a unit, it comes down to finding your flow and finding your rhythm as a unit and going out there and executing at a high level. We didn't do that."

title: Report: Chiefs are "very interested" in a Tyreek Hill reunion
description: Last year, before then-Dolphins receiver Tyreek Hill suffered a serious knee injury, the Chiefs were interested in trading for him.
fullText:
Last year, before then-Dolphins receiver Tyreek Hill suffered a serious knee injury, the Chiefs were interested in trading for him. Now that he's available to be signed by anyone, the Chiefs are interested in signing him.

Via Mike Silver of The Athletic, the Chiefs are "very interested" in a reunion with Hill. The team, per Silver, has already reached out to Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, regarding the possibility of bringing Hill back.

The first question is Hill's health. Silver says he's targeting a return in November.

Hill posted "hm" on Twitter after Chiefs receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle. Receiver Rashee Rice injured a hamstring earlier in the game.

A fifth-round pick in 2016, the 32-year-old Hill spent six seasons in Kansas City. A big contract for receiver Davante Adams in March 2022 prompted Hill to seek a trade to a team that would pay him more.

He spent four years with the Dolphins.

As Silver explains, multiple Chiefs players endorsed Hill's potential return.

"That's out of my hands, but I know I'd love to have 'The Cheetah' back in this building," tight end Travis Kelce said. "He's a brother. He's one of those people who, when he sets his mind to something, he usually delivers. You saw that with Miami, when all the haters were saying he couldn't play and he went and had his best year. I'd be excited by what he could do (here)."

"I have no idea [if that would happen], but it'd be pretty cool," quarterback Patrick Mahomes said.

Defensive tackle Chris Jones was more blunt: "I hope we do. It'd be dangerous. . . . Dangerous!"

During a media tour in New Orleans prior to Super Bowl LIX, Hill admitted that he regrets leaving the Chiefs. If/when he's healthy, he could get a chance to return — fueling the effort to chase another Super Bowl ring.

title: Utah Mammoth lose their 1st game of the season
description: Rangers forward Will Cuylle laid a dangerous hit on Mammoth star Dylan Guenther on Sunday. Here’s why it’s so serious.
fullText:
For the first time ever, the Utah Mammoth have lost a game in the state of New York.

The team went 6-0-0 there in their first two seasons, beating the New York Rangers, New York Islanders and Buffalo Sabres every time they headed east. Ironically, that changed as soon as the Mammoth acquired star forwards from both the Rangers and the Islanders.

Sunday's visit to Madison Square Garden proved to be the Mammoth's first true test of the 2026-27 season. After missing the playoffs the last two seasons, the Rangers seem intent on changing their fortune — and they've looked like a team to beat thus far.

"I thought the effort was there. We worked hard, we competed, we battled," said Andrew Peeke, who scored his first goal as a Mammoth in the game. "... Just a little sloppy on some execution things. We made (goaltender Karel Vejmelka) have to stand on his head."

The Mammoth's problem came from odd-man rushes. They allowed two breakaways in the first period, plus a 3-on-0, a 3-on-1 and a handful of 2-on-1s throughout the game. Vejmelka bailed his team out on most of them, but he could only do so much.

GABE WITH THE REBOUND 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/eOh9epZNCn

Head coach André Tourigny gave his diagnosis after the game.

"We were impatient. We were forcing plays. Instead of reloading quickly and being above (the puck), we were forcing things. We were waiting to see if we would cut the play before we reloaded. (In this) league, there's no forgiveness," he said.

"Don't get me wrong: Our reloads is one of our strengths. ... If we don't reload properly, that will cost us."

In December 2011, Jack Jablonski, a high school hockey player in Minnesota, crashed head-first into the boards after taking a hit from behind, and it left him a quadriplegic.

That situation is not unique to Jablonski — it's a real danger in the game of hockey — which is why "boarding" is such a serious penalty.

Mammoth forward Dylan Guenther was on the receiving end of a similar hit Sunday, though he was fortunate to avoid Jablonski's outcome. Guenther had a split second to turn his body, giving his shoulder the brunt of the impact rather than his head.

The rulebook states that the onus is on the offending player to avoid the hit if his opponent is in a vulnerable position. However, it also lists several potential mitigating factors for the referees to consider when making the call:

The degree of the impact with the boards.

Whether it results in an injury to the face or the head.

Whether the check could have been avoided.

Whether the opponent put himself in a vulnerable position immediately before or during the check.

In this instance, Rangers forward Will Cuylle, who threw the hit, was not forced into a corner. He was not off-balance. He could have eased up on the hit. He chose not to, and instead risked the long-term health of another person.

Despite all that, Cuylle got nothing more than a slap on the wrist in the form of a minor penalty.

This was a dirty hit that has no place in hockey. The fact that this was only a 2-minute minor is an absolute joke.#TusksUp #NYR https://t.co/sxcnbFCLAl

The applicable mitigating factors in this instance were that Guenther did not sustain an injury and that he was slightly crouched when Cuylle initiated the hit.

Jack McBain, who roomed with Guenther the past two seasons, stood up for his teammate at his first opportunity, dropping the gloves. Cuylle is no stranger to fighting and held his own in the scrap.

Cuylle brushed it off after the game.

"Obviously they thought it was a dirty hit, so, I guess, just answer the bell," he said. "They challenged me, so (I had to) just stand up for myself. They've got to stand up for their guys. That's hockey. Happy to do it."

title: Austin Cindric feels like he’s right on the edge of winning
description: Austin Cindric has had two of his strongest finishes of the year the past two weeks, and believes he’s close to breaking through for a win
fullText:
Austin Cindric had another strong finish at Las Vegas Motor Speedway on Sunday, taking fourth place in the South Point 400 to secure his second straight top-five of the Chase.

While Cindric was in the hunt for much of the race, it was Chase Briscoe who took the checkered flag with Kyle Larson and Tyler Reddick the most threatening cars to take the win from him in the late laps.

Still, Cindric believes he is right on the cusp of securing a win, and given how the No. 2 team looked both this week and last, there's good reason to believe him.

"I feel like we had a car that was pretty good, and close to capable of winning today," Cindric said. "A lot of déjà vu from last week with the leaders fighting for the win, still giving us the shot there. Just proud of everybody on the No. 2 car, to be able to bring two really fast cars two weeks in a row and really start to execute really well throughout this stretch."

Cindric credited his team for improving over the weekend, as the No. 2 was seventh in qualifying but wound up leading the race for 33 laps, more than any driver other than Briscoe or Denny Hamlin.

"It wasn't an easy weekend. We didn't start the race necessarily as close as we needed to. We didn't start practice necessarily as close as we needed to. Guys worked on it all day, gave us some strengths that we didn't have before. It takes a great team. That's what it takes to be good at this level on a consistent basis. Just want to win."

It feels like Cindric is right there, and he'll get another chance to compete for a win next week as the Chase heads to Charlotte. While Cindric is 128 points off of the Chase lead and almost assuredly out of the title race, he's clearly doing his best racing at the right time of the year, and seems ready to turn one of his "so close" days into a victory.

title: Mason Miller's uncharacteristic 9th-inning struggles put Padres on the verge of playoff elimination
description: — Mason Miller's emergence as the best closer in the major leagues helped get San Diego into the playoffs.His uncharacteristic troubles in the ninth inning Sunday have the Padres on the brink of elimination.
fullText:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — Mason Miller's emergence as the best closer in the major leagues helped get San Diego into the playoffs.

His uncharacteristic troubles in the ninth inning Sunday have the Padres on the brink of elimination.

The two-time All-Star closer struggled with control, loading the bases in the ninth inning against Milwaukee with the first three walks of his postseason career as he tried to complete a six-out save.

Jackson Chourio followed with a walk-off, two-run single with two outs that dealt the Padres a 4-3 loss. San Diego went home in a 2-0 NL Division Series deficit heading into Game 3 Tuesday.

"I didn't do my job today, so instead of being here with a win and a series tie, we're in a hole," Miller said.

Miller's unsuccessful attempt at his first six-out save since 2024 came one day after Adrian Morejon gave up a tiebreaking homer to William Contreras in the seventh inning of a 3-2 defeat.

"Two really good games that didn't go our way," first baseman Ty France said. "Just go back home and play each game like it's our last."

San Diego's inability to protect two-run leads in each of these first two games is a notable turn of events for a team that could shorten games much of the season because of its deep corps of relief pitchers.

The hard-throwing Miller led the bullpen brigade by collecting 38 saves and posting a 1.67 ERA while striking out 129 batters over 70 innings in the regular season. He threw 34 2/3 straight scoreless innings at one point in the season.

Miller hadn't been as dominant lately. He had an 0.79 ERA at the end of July before posting a 3.33 ERA from Aug. 1 through the end of the regular season. Even so, Miller's presence has given the Padres a sense of security they can maintain any late-inning lead.

Miller retired the side in order with a pair of strikeouts in the eighth inning and got the leadoff batter in the ninth with San Diego ahead 3-2.

That's when the problems started.

Christian Yelich walked on five pitches and stole second. Sal Frelick walked on a 3-2 pitch. After Miller retired Andrew Vaughn on a fly to center, Gary Sánchez walked while taking six straight pitches.

Chourio fell behind 1-2 in the count, fouled off Miller's fasted pitch of the day at 103.5 mph, then took a low slider before lining a 101.3 mph offering just past past second baseman Jake Cronenworth's attempt for a diving backhand stop and went into center field.

Although Miller threw 40 pitches — his most since 2023 — he said that didn't impact him and that he had felt fine. He topped 100 mph with 18 pitches.

"It's not the first save I've blown and it probably won't be the last one I blow, either," Miller said. "It's part of the job. Failure in my role is really hard to move past, I guess, when you look at it, because most of the time, when you fail, you lose. Other spots, you get another chance. That's part of it. I'm going to come back and be prepared to pitch Tuesday and do my best to help the team win."

San Diego remains confident it came rebound, If the Padres do, Miller likely would play a major role.

"He's been unbelievable ever since he put on a Padre uniform," pitcher Michael King said. "I know everybody in this locker room wants him with the ball in a big situation — and still does."

title: Philadelphia Eagles' Offense Sputters in Week 4 Loss to Rams
description: The Philadelphia Eagles' offense struggled in Week 4 in their loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles dropped to 2-2 with a 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. It was a rough game for the Eagles, particularly on the offensive side of the ball.

Philadelphia entered the game without star wide receiver DeVonta Smith and right tackle Lane Johnson, which made it tough for the offense. The injury news didn't get any better for the Eagles, as star running back Saquon Barkley left with a hamstring injury in the first quarter.

Tank Bigsby stepped up as the lead back for Philadelphia, rushing for 55 yards on 14 carries. However, it wasn't a strong performance overall, as the Eagles rushed for 104 yards on 27 carries as a team and didn't find the end zone.

The passing attack wasn't much better, as Jalen Hurts completed 12 of 27 passes for 98 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Darius Cooper was the leading receiver for Philadelphia with three receptions for 33 yards and two touchdowns. Although Cooper showed flashes of his talent, it was overall a terrible display from the offense.

While the offense struggled mightily, the Eagles' defense played at a high level. Cooper DeJean and Andrew Mukuba both picked off Matthew Stafford and held the Rams' elite offense to 10 points through the first three quarters.

However, with the offense struggling to get on the scoreboard, Philadelphia's defense couldn't hold strong forever. In the fourth quarter, Stafford led a 10-play, 97-yard drive that culminated in a one-yard touchdown run by Kyren Williams, which cut the Eagles' lead to 20-17.

After a three-and-out by the Eagles offense, Los Angeles got the ball back and took full advantage. Stafford led a 10-play, 79-yard drive, with Williams punching it into the end zone on a seven-yard run. That gave the Rams a 24-20 lead with 1:10 left in the game.

Philadelphia had a chance to take the lead, but it went nowhere. Byron Young sacked Hurts on first down, which wasted a ton of time as the Eagles were without timeouts.

On 2nd-and-17, Hurts threw an incompletion intended for Cooper. Young sacked Hurts again on third down, setting up a desperation fourth-down pass that fell incomplete.

The Eagles offense has looked atrocious through the first four games of the season, despite winning two. While they have injuries to key players, Philadelphia's issues go beyond that, and first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion needs to get the unit on track in Week 5 against a talented Jacksonville Jaguars team.

title: Down to their last strike, Jackson Chourio and the Brewers find a way in NLDS Game 2: 'One of my favorite games I’ve been a part of'
description: The fans in Milwaukee didn't have a whole lot to cheer about for 8 2/3 innings. Then Chourio delivered.
fullText:
MILWAUKEE — More than 41,000 Brewers fans had little to celebrate going into the ninth inning of Game 2 of the NLDS on Sunday. As a matter of fact, they were probably frustrated most of the game. For eight innings, their Brewers had looked unrecognizable. Eight innings of sloppy baseball, including three errors and two unearned runs, combined with a lack of offense had the Brewers on the brink of losing their first game of this postseason to the San Diego Padres. And against MLB's best and most intimidating closer, Mason Miller, things looked grim.

Then the Brewers remembered who they are. It might've taken 8 2/3 innings, but in their 4-3 walkoff victory over the Padres in Game 2, they gave a sellout crowd at American Family Field a reason to cheer and a game they'll never forget.

"One of my favorite games I've been a part of," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. "And what's most gratifying to see is how many of our great fans came out to see that one. Just happy for the club, happy for the city that they got to witness something so special."

But let's back up. Before Milwaukee could attempt to walk off the Padres, they first had to tie the game against Miller after entering the ninth down 3-2. And that required baserunners. Up to that point, San Diego had allowed very little traffic, and the Brewers had mustered just four hits prior to the ninth. But with the Brewers down to their final three outs, newly minted captain Christian Yelich worked a five-pitch walk against Miller to put the tying run on first base with one out.

Of course, one at-bat alone doesn't make for a comeback against the game's best reliever. But for a team like the Brewers, who have always believed as an organization that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts, the mindset was to keep the line moving.

"Just grind, man. Just find a way to get on there," Yelich said afterward. "Doesn't matter if it's a walk or a hit. We just want some traffic in that inning there, and just see what happens."

After drawing that walk, Yelich handed the baton to Sal Frelick. Frelick fell behind in the count 1-2 against Miller, a place no hitter wants to be. But then the Brewers' right fielder buckled down, taking three straight Miller pitches to draw another walk.

"Guys like that don't give up multiple hits in innings very often," Frelick said. "He was tasked with six outs today, so wanted to kind of get pressure on him, see if we could get some guys on."

Following an Andrew Vaughn flyout for the second out, arguably the biggest at-bat of the ninth came from catcher Gary Sánchez, who pinch hit for David Hamilton. Sánchez is on the Brewers' NLDS roster for moments like this — opportunities for a big swing. But just like his teammates, the veteran wasn't necessarily looking for a three-run shot.

Like Yelich and Frelick before him, Sánchez was able to grind and put together another tough at-bat against Miller. After working the count full, he drew the Brewers' third walk of the inning.

"He's the best in the game," first baseman Jake Bauers said of Miller before the series. "I think the mentality is try to have a good at-bat. Whatever happens after that is whatever happens."

Jackson Chourio's moment. #NoTimeLikeOctober pic.twitter.com/7yJ4ttQaqj

What happened is Milwaukee's biggest star came up in the biggest moment. With the bases loaded and two out in the bottom of the ninth, who else would step into the box but Jackson Chourio?

Having announced his presence in this series with a game-tying, two-run shot in the Brewers' Game 1 victory, Chourio had plenty of confidence going into his at-bat against Miller. And the 22-year-old wasn't trying to play here. He understood exactly what was unfolding.

"Watching those at-bats beforehand, I knew that he was a little bit erratic," Chourio said of Miller. "He was throwing some balls. I knew that he was gonna come at me with the fastball at some point, so mentally, I was just making sure that I was prepared for that."

The first two times Miller came at Chourio with the fastball, it worked; Chourio swung-and-missed at 100.8 mph and 102.2 mph before fouling off 103.5 mph. But after taking a tough slider to make it a 2-2 count, Chourio decided to call game.

Miller offered a 101.3 mph fastball, and Chourio ripped a 109.5 mph single into center field, past a diving Jake Cronenworth. Yelich scored easily from third, and as a flying Frelick slid across home plate to beat the throw from center fielder Jackson Merrill, the crowd let out a collective roar.

"I think it's probably in the top three of the special moments I've had in my career," Chourio said afterward.

FULL AT-BAT: Jackson Chourio vs. Mason Miller 🍿

The Brewers walk it off to take a 2-0 lead in the NLDS! pic.twitter.com/muBNJw1YKw

Since he made his Major League debut at just 20 years old, the Brewers have known that Chourio is special. After his first three seasons in the big leagues, with him already having monster postseason numbers, that bar might not be high enough. Milwaukee's young superstar is taking his game to an even higher level.

"I think he's been that type of player. The talent is undeniable when you watch him play," Yelich said of Chourio. "There's nothing he can't do on the baseball field. The more experience he gets, the more situations he's in, the more he kind of learns the league and just racks up the at-bats, he's just going to continue to get better.

"And that's kind of scary because he's pretty good right now."

Said Murphy: "He's starting to realize how he has to play the game. As talented as he is, he's still learning the game. … As a hitter, when he stays under control, it's amazing. He's, I think, turning into a bona fide, top-flight player. Couldn't be happier for him because he brings it every day."

With Chourio's heroics, the Brewers take a commanding 2-0 NLDS lead on the Padres and will head to San Diego one win away from returning to the NLCS. By winning a game Sunday in which they didn't play anywhere close to their best until the very end, this team showed that they can find a way no matter what.

"It's the attention to detail that is instilled in our culture, stuff that I learned from [Yelich] when I first got called up," Frelick said. "If you're not doing it, you don't play."

"It's a team that's unified," Chourio said. "We know what our strengths are, and we know how to support each other. … Everyone's supporting each other, and we know how to win."

title: Marquette Topples Creighton In Five Sets
description: The Golden Eagles scrape together enough points to beat the Bluejays on the road for the first time in over five years.
fullText:
And just like that, everyone in the Big East has one loss after four matches of conference play.

Sunday's Marquette/Creighton match was the last contest in the cycle to get everyone to four matches played. Going into Saturday's contests, we were down to Creighton and Butler with a zero in the loss column, and St. John's took care of business there, 3-1, leaving the Bluejays as the last unbeaten in the league as of Sunday morning.

And for a second there, probably several seconds there in Omaha, it looked like Creighton was going to be able to say that on Monday morning, too. The Bluejays took the first set from Marquette, 25-16, holding the Golden Eagles to just .114 hitting and rolling past them at a .343 clip. It was 5-0 Bluejays before anyone blinked, and MU couldn't get closer than three points. Another 5-0 run made it 20-12, and thus academic.

Creighton broke open some four point leads in the second set but Marquette was able to overcome those this time. It was tightly contested, all the way up to a misfire from Carson Tyler bringing the Jays within one, 23-22, but Caydence Doolan got the call and put down the final two points to even the match at one set each.

The Jays got out to a little lead early in the third, but this time Marquette wasn't quite as successful at powering through. The lead hit five, then six, then seven at 20-13, and yep, trouble town. The Golden Eagles scrapped together a few more points, but Ashlyn Paymal recorded a kill to make it 25-17, and that's two kind of lopsided Creighton wins against a hard fought Marquette win. That's a bad sign for a MU team that now needed to win the fourth in order to just get to a fifth set to try to beat the Jays. That's a bad sign for a Marquette team that hasn't done well when things have gone past three sets this season.

This time it was Marquette with the 4-0 lead out of the gate. That sounds encouraging, but Eloise Brandewie knotted the set at seven and an error by Tyler gave the Bluejays the lead. Tied at 10, then Marquette snapped off a 6-0 run. That was just enough space for Marquette to get to 25 before Creighton caught up with them, and an attack error by Ayden Ames gave the Golden Eagles the chance they needed.

Tied at 5, tied at 7, tied at 8, tied at 10, 11, 12, and 13. Remember, fifth set. First to 15, win by two. The last two ties, it was Creighton going up one and Marquette wiping it out on the next point.

Same thing again, tied at 14, extra points now required to win.

Same AGAIN, tied at 17. Four match points fended off by Marquette here.

Block by Luanna Markus and Julia Stanev… Marquette up 18-17?

S5 | MU 19 – Creighton 17

MU DEFEATS CREIGHTON ON THE ROAD IN 5 SETS!#WeAreMarquette | #MarquetteVB pic.twitter.com/Fzcfa2LfBJ

After a wild recovery free return from Creighton because of a Marquette rejection, Avery Helms camped underneath, sent it up to Markus for a swing from Tyler. She sent it hard into the Creighton block, which is not necessarily a good thing, but in this case, her shot went off the block, out of bounds on MU's side, Match Point Marquette, and the Golden Eagles have won a regularly timed regular season match at Creighton for the first time since 2011. It is just the eighth win in program history against Creighton, and it snaps a seven match winning streak in the series by the Bluejays.

And honestly? Marquette wasn't very good here. For the match, they hit just .160 against .286 from Creighton. All three of Marquette's hitters with more than 20 swings in the match hit under .160. Shouts to Molly Welge, who had eight kills and no errors on 19 attempts for a .421 day. Marquette couldn't do a thing to slow down Ashlyn Paymal or Eloise Brandewie, both of whom had 15+ kills and hit over .370. But they did close down Ayden Ames, who ended up hitting just .186 while tying with Abbey Hayes for the most swings from the Bluejays. Of note along the way here: Remember in the preview when I said that Trinity Shadd-Ceres was averaging a team high 3.05 kills and leading the team in total attacks, but she wasn't quite at that level last weekend?

Four swings while playing in all five sets. Hey, Creighton: Whatcha doin'?

How about some highlights, courtesy of GoMarquette.com and ESPN+?

Next weekend's encounters will be against Georgetown at 7pm Central time on Friday and against Villanova at 5pm Central on Saturday, with ESPN+ taking the broadcast on both. Saturday's the big one, as it's the official ceremony for Tat Shiely and Allie Barber as the first two volleyball banners up in the McGuire Center.

The Hoyas are 10-5 on the year but 2-2 in the Big East after beating UConn and Providence at home this weekend, while the Wildcats are just 9-6 after starting the year earning AVCA top 25 votes, and they did exactly what Georgetown did to get to 2-2 in conference play.

title: Red Sox Must Lock Up Adley Rutschman Before Winter Ends
description: The Red Sox face a massive contract decision on Adley Rutschman. Yahoo Sports says a $30 million option is a drop-dead deadline. Read why an extension is vital.
fullText:
The Boston Red Sox face their biggest test this winter. They must decide on a contract for Adley Rutschman. SI reports that the team gave up a lot to get him. If they do not sign him now, the deal could look like a total failure. The window to fix this is open right now.

Time is the enemy here. Rutschman is under team control for only one more season. After the 2027 season, he becomes a free agent. The Red Sox cannot let him walk away. The cost of losing him after such a big trade would be too high.

The club should do everything to keep him. The free agent market is weak this year. This makes it the perfect time to make a move. A deal signed now would cost a lot of money, but it would secure a star for the core group.

Many fans are watching the mutual option for Sonny Gray. A mutual option worth $30 million is certain to be declined by him. This is a simple choice. The team will not pay that price. It is just a formality before looking for a new deal later.

The real drama is not about Gray. It is about the catcher position. The Red Sox have struggled to find a star backstop for years. They finally have one. Rutschman is an All-Star and a positive addition to the organization. He was excellent defensively in the second half.

His bat was slow to start after he came off the Injured List. But he got hot in September. He proved he can handle the pressure. The team needs to build on that success. Letting him go now would be a disaster.

The price paid to get Rutschman was very high. The Baltimore Orioles received an arm and a leg from the Red Sox. That trade was made ahead of the 2026 trade deadline. If the team only keeps him for a little over one full season, the trade looks bad.

Reports say the situation should have every fan's attention. Rutschman is 28 years old. He is young enough to fit the future core. When he is healthy, he is a game-changer. The team needs to lock him in before the clock runs out.

The club should be prepared to offer an extension this winter. It will not be cheap. A big contract might change how the team handles the rest of the offseason. But the risk of losing a star is worse than the cost.

The free agent class is very weak. This is a key reason to act. Similar players like Garrett Crochet and Roman Anthony are in line for deals. Rutschman should be next. The Red Sox cannot wait for the market to get better.

The roster is arguably better than last year. But the playoff run ended early again. The team has time to prepare for 2027. They need to use that time wisely. Fixing the contract situation is the first step.

title: Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty injured ankle still not right and it shows
description: Even though Ashton Jeanty has played every game this season, he is clearly not back full from the ankle injury he suffered in camp.
fullText:
When Ashton Jeanty went down in practice during training camp, the initial fear was the worst. The first news back from that was good, because it wasn't a serious knee injury, but rather a sprained ankle. Even then, ankles can be tricky. The severity can vary quite a bit, and with three weeks until the start of the season, there was uncertainty whether the second-year back would be ready to go.

The fears of the ankle severity were put to bed when not only was he active for the season opener, but had a put up 103 yards on 23 carries. Since then those fears have been jolted out awake like a fire drill in the middle of the night.

In the three games since then, he has averaged under three yards per carry, including Sunday against the Chiefs where Jeanty had 58 yards on 15 carries and at one point hobbled off the field in pain and stayed sidelined for a time.

"I'm feeling all right," Jeanty said after the game. "I mean, just gotta get back to work, and keep rehabbing and keep making it stronger."

It can be difficult to rehab an injury when he constantly running on it. The fact that this is the second game in a row he's had obvious issues with his ankles shows that without a doubt. Week two in LA he had his worst game, averaging just 2.3 yards per carry, and last week in New Orleans he was clearly struggling on it and had to get it taped up.

In that regard, I guess his 3.9 yards per carry against the Chiefs is a step up. And there were flashes, such as his 19-yard run and his 28-yard catch and run.

"It's getting stronger, and I feel like I'm gonna be 100% real soon," Jeanty added.

The Raiders are really hoping that's true. Because they really need him. The Patriots are up next and they are beatable, but it may take more of a contribution from their former sixth overall pick to do it.

title: New York Jets: Slip Sliding Away
description: Aaron Glenn is at a crossroads. What happens next is critical for his, and the Jets’, future.
fullText:
The New York Jets got the 2026 season off to a rousing start as they dominated the Tennessee Titans on their way to a 23 – 10 opening day victory. It was their first win since November 30, 2025, and only their third double digit win since the 2023 season. It has been a long time since the Jets have looked dominant. Unfortunately, it didn't last.

Since that big opening day win the Jets' fortunes have been gradually sliding downhill. They dominated the Titans all game in week 1. In week 2 the Jets dominated the Green Bay Packers for 49 minutes before they collapsed and allowed 13 unanswered points to close the game in an overtime loss. In week 3 against the Detroit Lions the Jets never dominated, but they kept the game close and were in position to tie the score late before Geno Smith lost a fumble on the Jets' final drive of the game. In week 4 against the Chicago Bears the Jets were thoroughly dominated from start to finish in a 23 – 12 loss that was not nearly as competitive as the final score might indicate.

The trend here is not encouraging. The Jets have gotten less competitive with each passing game, culminating in a game against the Bears on Sunday where the Bears outgained the Jets by well over 300 yards and the Bears had more first downs on offense than the Jets offense had plays. That is annihilation.

The loss brought the Jets 2026 record to 1-3. Playoff hopes are already growing faint, as teams starting the season 1-3 have only made the playoffs a little over 13% of the time since the 2012 season.

For Aaron Glenn the loss was his 17th in a little more than a year as Jets head coach. He has a 4-17 record overall, good for a .190 winning percentage. The Aaron Glenn Jets have lost 8 of their last 9 games and 10 of their last 12. That is a very troubling record.

The Jets have had 13 head coaches who have coached the team at least two full seasons. In chronological order they are as follows:

Of these 13 head coaches, only Rich Kotite had fewer wins than Glenn after 21 games. Kotite was arguably the worst head coach in Jets history, and one of the worst in NFL history.

Only two of these 13 Jets head coaches had less than 10 wins after two seasons: Rich Kotite and Adam Gase. Both were fired after two seasons with the team. For Glenn to get to 10 wins over two seasons he would need to win at least six of the remaining 13 games in the 2026 season.

Glenn has a .190 winning percentage in his head coaching career with the Jets. Just one Jets head coach has ever been worse in his first two years: Rich Kotite.

Glenn's Jets had a -203 point differential in his first season as Jets head coach. Not even the lowly Kotite ever posted a worse point differential. In fact there has only been one worse season in Jets history. Adam Gase posted a -214 point differential in his 2-14 2020 campaign. He was promptly fired.

The Jets season looks like it is already slipping away. Glenn's career as Jets head coach may follow suit. It is difficult at this point to identify much that Glenn has excelled at. It is not difficult to point to areas in which he has struggled. With three more first round draft picks in the 2027 draft soon to be made and the Jets very likely selecting a quarterback with one of them, can the Jets afford to allow the Glenn regime to make those picks if we don't soon see a major turnaround? Six first round picks in two years represent an historic opportunity for a quick turnaround. It would be a major disappointment if the team invested a regime that has shown little chance of success thus far with that opportunity.

The Jets have had just 13 playoff seasons in their 66 year history. Only two of them involved a start with 1 or fewer wins in the first four games of the season. It happened in the 1991 season when the Jets improbably sneaked into the playoffs with an 8-8 record with a dramatic overtime victory over the Miami Dolphins on the last day of the regular season. They were then unceremoniously bounced out of the playoffs with a loss in the Wild Card round. The Jets did not return to the playoffs for seven years after that loss.

If you're looking for a silver lining, here it is. In 1981 the Jets had not made the playoffs since the 1969 season, an 11 year drought that was the longest in Jets history until the current 15 year streak. The Jets hadn't had a winning season during that 11 year stretch, a streak that exceeds any other such stretch in Jets history, including the current 10 year streak.

That 1981 Jets team was led by first time head coach Walt Michaels, who had never posted a winning record in his first four seasons as Jets head coach. The 1981 season gave no indications it would be different after the first four games. The Jets opened the 1981 season with a 31 – 0 blowout loss to the Buffalo Bills. After three games the Jets were 0-3 with a -60 point differential. The season was threatening to spiral out of control.

Then something clicked. The Jets won in week 4. That started a 10 game stretch in which the Jets lost just one game. By the end of the season the Jets were 10-5-1 and in the playoffs for the first time since 1969. They lost in the Wild Card round to the Buffalo Bills, but that 1981 season was the beginning of the legendary New York Sack Exchange Jets. Seemingly overnight the LOL Jets were transformed into a force to be reckoned with. They went on to make the playoffs four of the next six years, the best sustained stretch of Jets football in their history. Eventually the Sack Exchange grew old and broke up, and the Jets entered a decade of terrible football from the late 1980s through the late 1990s. But for a short time in the early to mid 1980s the Jets were a dangerous football team, led by a head coach in Walt Michaels who had never had a winning season before the turnaround.

Can Aaron Glenn follow in Walt Michaels' footsteps and usher in a new era of sustained Jets success? Based on what we've seen from him thus far, it doesn't seem likely. But Michael's dramatic turnaround in 1981 seemed just as unlikely after four games of the 1981 season. Then everything changed.

Whether Glenn has it in him to engineer such a turnaround is the question the Jets must answer this season. Right now the season, and Glenn's Jets career, appear to be slip sliding away. Time is running out for Glenn to change this. If we don't see major progress soon, the Jets will need to once again move on and start over.

title: Everything Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said following Week 4 loss to Cowboys
description: Here's everything Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said following Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, including the team's 0-4 start, the lack of a run game and where the team can go from here in hopes of saving the season.
fullText:
Here's everything Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said following Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, including the team's 0-4 start, the lack of a run game and where the team can go from here in hopes of saving the season.

Question: On the defense struggling to finish out games

DeMeco Ryans: "Yeah, today it was not a great finish by our team defensively. It was not good enough. If the offense goes out and plays like they played to give us 30 points, defensively you have to find a way to close that game out. It was disappointing that we've been in three games that way where the offense has done a great job and we haven't been able to close it out there in the second half. We've got to look at it all and see what changes we need to make and what we need to fix."

Q: On Dallas Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb having a big game

Ryans: "We have to play our technique better. In the second half it just wasn't good enough. First half, I thought everybody played the coverages the proper way. They were where they were supposed to be, eliminated the explosive plays. From the second half, whatever the reason that may be, we did not do our coverages the proper way."

Ryans: "The penalties definitely crushed us today. Too many self-inflicted penalties offensively. We had penalties to start the drive, kickoff return. Way too many penalties hurting the team, not helping the team. Defensively, third down. We had a lot of things that we're fighting against ourselves and you can't win football in the NFL that way when you're constantly fighting the uphill battle. So, the penalties have to be eliminated."

"The offense scored 30 points."

Ryans: "I have to look at the film and see what happened, but in a couple of plays there where you see CeeDee is just wide open; that's definitely not our plan. We have to look at it to see what happened, what were the communication miscues that happened, but that's not how we play coverage."

Q: On QB C.J. Stroud dealing with offensive penalties and other offensive mistakes

Ryans: "C.J. is a big boy. He played outstanding today, threw the ball around really well. It was great having Nico back. Would love to be able to celebrate Nico for him being back, creating explosive plays there to start the football game, to get in the end zone two times. Jaylin Noel stepped up. Big, explosive play on offense. Also, big, explosive kick return as well. There were a lot of great things. 'KB' [Kayshon Boutte] continues to make tough, contested catches time and time again. [Xavier] Hutchison showed up big-time on some third downs, some catch-and-run-type plays, creating first downs, keeping the chains moving. Many positive things that I would love to highlight from our guys offensively. They did a really great job. Whether it's running the ball, throwing the ball, it didn't matter. Our guys moved the ball really well. It just didn't play well enough defensively, and it's a bad feeling. You don't play that well defensively to finish a game when the offense did such an outstanding job, right? That's just not great on our part."

Ryans: "You stick together, and you keep going. That's what it is. All these games, we've been in these games. We just got to find a way to finish these games. That's what it is. It's 0-4, that's our record. That's what it says who we are right now, but how do you come out of it, it's what I told our guys, you stick together. There's no pointing fingers, no blaming. 'Hey, you look within yourself. [Head Coach] DeMeco [Ryans], what do you have to do better to get it corrected?' That's where I start with myself. How can I get it all corrected?"

Q: On the difference between the first and second half defensively

Ryans: "I have to look at it to see exactly what happened. For us, I know they came out, we gave up the big return to start the second half, which we can't do. We have to cover better there on special teams, and then we allowed them to go down and score. They're in range now, so have to look at it again to see. I know in the second half we gave up way too many explosive plays. If we want to stop an explosive offense like that, you can't allow the ball to be completed 20 yards more down the field. We gave up way too many of those to good players. Did a good job in the first half, but for whatever reason it is, I'll have to examine it on the video this evening and see what happened."

Q: On opponents generating explosive plays

Ryans: "We'll look at the film and see what really happened on the explosive plays, but there is no coverage where we designed to leave guys open. That's not a coverage, so we have to do a better job there. They made a play. I thought it was George [Pickens] made a really big play there, that's a contested play right there. Kamari [Lassiter] is battling, a contested play today made. We have to find a way to be on the other side of this, find a way to get the ball out, find a way to get the quarterback down."

Ryans: "Whatever. I mean, it's my job as the leader of this football team to do whatever it takes for us to turn this thing around."

Q: On the message to the team postgame

Ryans: "It's the same message. The only people that can do anything about the 0-4 start are the guys in that locker room. Coaches, players, we all have to stick together. It's easy when you are in this spot to point fingers or blame this person or that person. That doesn't solve anything. When things get hard, adversity hits, you climb your way through it by sticking together. That's the only way I know. Been there, done it. That's the only way I know and we'll keep working. We'll get back to the drawing board, keep working, but a lot of guys did a lot of good things today. A lot of good things. My message is it hurts me that I can't go in and celebrate those positives that a lot of guys showed today on the field for us."

"I'll have to look at the film to see what happened there."

Q: On the biggest difference from last year's start to this year's

Ryans: "I understand a lot of people want to compare 2025 to 2026, but for me, it's not the same. It's not. We got a different team. We have different people, it's different. As much as we would love 2025 to carry over into 2026, that's never the case. That never works in the NFL. Just because you have prior success, that doesn't automatically mean you're going to have future success. You have to go out and earn everything you get in the NFL and right now we're not doing the things to earn the right to win games. So when we do things the proper way, and we put the work in the proper way, we close games out how we're supposed to close it out. You have to go earn it. Nobody is handing us any wins. We'll get a win when we go earn it the right way."

Q: On if the players thought 2025 was going to carry over into this season

Ryans: "You would have to ask the guys individually on that, but for me, every year you start over. For me, 2025 was 2025. It's a shame we're sitting here talking about that right now, but for us, 2026, what do we do about it right now? That's my mindset. That's the mindset of our players."

Q: On the pass interference call that lead to a Cowboys touchdown

Ryans: "That was a tough one for us there in the red zone. I thought our guys played it tight. It was tough and the energy was right from our crowd. The fans were definitely into it. Man, I wanted that stop there on fourth down, but unfortunately, we didn't get the stop. I don't control what happens there with the penalties, but man, our guys battled there. I thought we were clean. Came away with the stop there, but it didn't go our way."

title: Durzi bragging rights among key takeaways from Rangers win over Mammoth
description: That New York Rangers’ 4-2 win over the Utah Mammoth on Sunday at Madison Square Garden was super entertaining. The […]
fullText:
That New York Rangers' 4-2 win over the Utah Mammoth on Sunday at Madison Square Garden was super entertaining. The game was played at a frenetic pace, with plenty of physicality, scoring chances aplenty, a slew of breakaways, and one big-time save after another from goaltenders Igor Shesterkin and Karel Vejmelka.

There'll be things the Rangers want to clean up and get better at after watching the video from this one. But you can bet there wasn't a single fan at MSG that didn't have a good time Sunday, nor was displeased at all with the winning results against a very good opponent.

The Rangers (3-1-0) have won three in a row, including both their games played at The Garden, so far. These Rangers have many of the same faces on the roster, but they sure don't seem like the 2025-26 Rangers.

"I just like how we're coming together as a group … It's a good feeling we have," coach Mike Sullivan said afterward. "We've won a couple of games. These guys are playing hard. They're paying the price to win, whether it be blocking shots or winning puck battles, things of that nature. But I'm really excited and couldn't be more proud of the guys just for the team game that we're building. And I think part of that is just the chemistry inside of the locker that continues to grow and evolve."

Will Cuylle was a menace physically out there, racking up 11 penalty minutes and nearly setting off a riot in the second period when he boarded Dylan Guenther. Then to start the third period, he answered the bell, accepting Jack McBain's invite to fight. Two minutes after that rousing fight, Gabe Perreault buried a rebound to snap a 1-1 tie.

WOWZA 🤩

Gabe Perreault gives the @NYRangers the lead! pic.twitter.com/QNslu0P05q

J.T. Miller finally was rewarded for consistently going to the net this season when Vladislav Gavrikov's shot hit off his skate and into the net at 12:47 of the third period. Gavrikov had a monster game and was selected First Star, scoring his first goal of the season in the opening period, assisting on Miller's tally, and blocking a team-high four shots at the other end of the ice.

It wasn't always pretty. But it was fun. And it was a good win.

You know Sean Durzi and Vincent Trocheck had this game circled on their calendars, as the old cliche goes. The Rangers acquired Durzi from the Mammoth on July 1 in a trade that sent Trocheck out west, and both teams appear pleased with the deal.

As for the individuals Sunday, Trocheck received the expected video tribute during the first TV timeout, to go along with an extended standing ovation from the fans at MSG. He also was minus-three and his team lost the game.

Welcome back to The Garden, Troch 💙❤️ pic.twitter.com/qAeLpmzKgl

— New York Rangers (@NYRangers) October 4, 2026

Durzi delivered a perfect open-ice hip check that wiped Trocheck out in the neutral zone just five minutes into the game. The 27-year-old defenseman logged 22:57 TOI against his former team, blocked three shots, and was plus-one. And the Rangers won the game.

So, for one night at least, bragging rights go to Durzi. Let's see what happens in the rematch in Salt Lake City on March 9.

#NYR Sean Durzi on playing against Vinny Trocheck and beating his former team tonight: 

"It was funny — I got a pretty good piece of him early on in the first and then I think he got a lick at me and he said 'that's just payback' — so it was funny out there. We had dinner… pic.twitter.com/jHI48wXvES

— Jonny Lazarus (@JLazzy23) October 5, 2026

Alexis Lafreniere remains without a goal through four games, but with any luck he could've had three or maybe more Sunday in his best outing of the young season. The soon-to-be 25-year-old constantly got behind the Mammoth defense for one Grade-A scoring chance after another. Vejmelka found every possible way to stop the Rangers forward, who also ripped a power-play shot off the crossbar in the final seconds of the first period.

Lafreniere did pick up his first assist of the season, though. He was flat-out robbed again by Vejmelka on a 2-on-1 set up by a perfect Mika Zibanejad pass, but with the goalie out of position, Perreault cleaned up for the go-ahead goal in the third period.

He led the Rangers with nine shot attempts and four shots on goal, logged 21:44 TOI, and had his coach raving about a blocked shot Lafreniere made in the final minutes of regulation.

So, Laf just has to laugh about not scoring a goal Sunday. He keeps getting these chances, you know the puck's going to start going in for him.

Playing his first game since recording the first goalie goal in Rangers history, Shesterkin was encouraged by the raucous Blueshirt Faithful every time he touched the puck it seemed to shoot it down the ice. And though Shesterkin didn't score another goal Sunday, he did shoot for the empty net after the Mammoth pulled Vejmelka for a sixth attacker in the closing minutes.

His attempt was picked off near the Mammoth blue line; but Shesterkin did add to his point total by assisting on Eeli Tolvanen's empty-net goal shortly thereafter at 18:45 of the third period. The Rangers netminder zipped the puck up to Cuylle to start the scoring play, giving him a point in two straight games.

"I thought it was pretty funny when they were yelling 'shoot' in the first period when [the Mammoth] still had the goalie in the net," Cuylle said postgame.

Oh, and Shesterkin was also really good at the other part of his game, the one the Rangers pay him to be the richest goalie in NHL history. Shesterkin made 27 saves, including a few point-blank beauties and 13 in the third period. He now has a 1.67 goals-against average and .934 save percentage in three starts this season.

The Rangers lost center Joe Veleno to a lower-body injury midway through the first period, and played the rest of the way without the 4C, who's also one of their top penalty killers. Since the Rangers really don't have the luxury of having a winger who's also accustomed to — and capable of — playing center, they largely split those fourth-line shifts between the centers they already had in the lineup.

Third-line center Noah Laba logged a season-high 17:37 TOI, and Zibanejad played 24:32, more than any skater on either team Sunday. Sullivan also shortened his bench in the third period — fourth-liners Oliver Bjorkstrand (three) and Jaroslav Chmelar (two) had just a handful of shifts.

Laba won 6 of 10 face-offs, was credited with two hits, and was plus-one. However, his underlying numbers weren't great — he had an expected goal share 5v5 of 10.53 percent, per Natural Stat Trick. The Rangers were out-shot 14-2 with him on the ice 5v5.

Since their extra forward again was Matt Rempe, the Rangers likely need to recall a center from Hartford of the American Hockey League if Veleno is to miss any games because of his injury. Though they'd probably prefer a veteran center like Justin Dowling or Juuso Parssinen stepping in this early in the season to fill in, it's worth noting 20-year-old Cole Beaudoin has five points (one goal, four assists) in his first two games as a pro with Hartford.

title: Kentucky Football made some absurd history with AP Top 25 Poll snub
description: The Cats win on the road in the SEC and still fall out of the AP Top 25.
fullText:
Despite being ranked 24th and going on the road to defeat South Carolina, Kentucky Football fell out of the AP Top 25 poll.

It came across as pretty odd when the poll was released, and as it turns out, Kentucky's situation is pretty rare when it comes to college football history.

According to Lee K. Howard from WKYT, it's only the 4th time in 90 years that a Power 4 team won a conference road game while ranked and still fell out of the AP Top 25.

Kentucky actually gained points in the poll, going from 150 to 160, but Pittsburgh finished with two more votes, giving them the final nod in the rankings.

Going on the road and winning in the SEC is tough, even against teams toward the bottom of the conference, so Kentucky's win against South Carolina shouldn't be diminished, especially since the Gamecocks were the betting favorite heading into kickoff and even were a touchdown favorite at one point.

Hopefully Will Stein and his Wildcats can use the rankings snub as motivation with a huge game coming up in Lexington on Saturday when Lane Kiffin and the 10th-ranked LSU Tigers come to town.

We can also take solace in the fact that ESPN senior writer Heather Dinich is a real one.

I have Kentucky No. 17 in my top 25. @UKFootball is no. 5 in ESPN strength of record metric. Two road wins vs SEC teams. I rank 25 teams based on what I think the CFP committee would do. And KY would probably be in.

Kentucky won on the road in conference play… and still fell out of the AP Poll. Only the 12th time a Power 4 team has done that since 1936.

UK even gained voting points this week (150 to 160), but Pitt's road win was enough to edge the Wildcats for the final spot by just two… pic.twitter.com/TBrZHaQP82

fullText:
Todd Bowles' take on being 0-4 has Buccaneers fans pushing him out door appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Fans are getting fed up with Todd Bowles despite his postgame comments following the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' 17-14 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday afternoon.

Bowles has been a head coach in the NFL for 10 seasons since his debut in 2011, going through his fifth year with the Buccaneers. Following three consecutive playoff appearances, the team missed out on the postseason in 2025.

This placed a spotlight on Bowles' job security, especially as anything less than playoff contention would put him at risk of a firing. It doesn't do him any favors after Tampa Bay fell to 0-4 on the season following the loss to Green Bay. The head coach reflected on the loss after the game, having frustration with the inability to close out games.

"Bowles said the team is losing close games and needs to learn how to finish them. It isn't frustrating because they're close, just that they're 0-4. Said the need for improvement starts with him," reporter Greg Auman wrote.

Fans are losing patience as they provided their thoughts on social media. Here are some of their reactions.

"Bowles needs to realize that being close isn't good enough… or even close to good enough. The teams we are losing to aren't going to be above .500 by the end of the season. We should be throttling them, not playing close," one fan said.

"He almost had it. The need for improvement starts with Getting Rid of him. As far as I am concerned this season is a win-win for Bucs Fans. Either they go on a epic and historic run or we finally, finally get rid of Bowles! Just pray they get ab Offensive HC so we can get some consistency around here," another remarked.

"It's insane he is okay saying that considering this is a very clear regression for this team. If this is your first or second year, fine but he's had way too long to figure it out to admit he doesn't know how to seal the deal," one commented.

The Buccaneers will look to bounce back in their next matchup, being on the road. They take on the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5 as kickoff commences on Oct. 8 at 8:15 p.m. ET.

title: Winners and Losers from Seahawks’ needlessly close win vs. Chargers
description: The Seahawks won as expected against the Chargers, but it was far from pretty.
fullText:
Hey, the Seattle Seahawks got a win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Was it borderline unwatchable because of all the penalties, punts, and the near collapse from a 27-6 lead to a 30-23 score? Yeah. Is it still a win? Yes it is. Given the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers both won, it was pretty important for the Seahawks to stay ahead of the Rams and not lose contact with San Francisco ahead of the big Week 5 showdown.

Let's get to Winners and Losers while this game is still etched in my brain.

Emanuel Wilson's first start is one of his best performances in the NFL

If I could give a game ball to anyone on the Seahawks offense, it's Emanuel Wilson. He had 81 hard-earned yards on 21 carries, his first Seahawks rushing TD, and he took a 23-yard screen pass (!) to the house. Over 100 scrimmage yards for Wilson on a day when Seattle's offense was far from crisp. He's not fast or particularly great with lateral quickness, but he runs hard and can play through contact well when he gets downhill.

Rashid Shaheed makes the most of his limited touches

Only three touches on offense for Shaheed, but one was a 28-yard touchdown run, another was a five-yard carry on a 1st and 10, and his lone reception was a 20-yard catch. Given his slow start to the season, he showed up in a major way even on a low volume of offensive plays. I thought he was agonizingly close to breaking a big punt return, too.

Tory Horton is back in the end zone

How about a touchdown for the first time since last year's Commanders game? It was Horton's only catch and only target, but it was a smooth slant on a Sam Darnold check at the line of scrimmage. Hopefully we see more of Horton in the offense as the weeks progress.

There was a real chance the Seahawks could've given up a tying touchdown, if not a winning touchdown on that final drive. Uchenna Nwosu closed the show by haunting his former team, strip-sacking Justin Herbert and sealing the win. Nwosu has played well throughout the season and now has the sack to show it, plus he's as good as it gets when it comes to edge-setting in the run game.

I would walk through walls for Ernest Jones IV

Ernest had a sack and an interception, and there's a chance he could end this weekend as the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for a phenomenal performance. The Seahawks defense (when they weren't getting flagged) stifled the Chargers offense, and Jones was a big part of that stifling. He's one of the leaders on the team and he is a premier inside linebacker.

Last week was not one of Thomas' better days at the office. He started this game with an interception on the first play from scrimmage, and had a TFL on a screen pass. Thomas is just a fireplug of a linebacker and is extremely fun to watch.

Nick Emmanwori looked like Nick Emmanwori, albeit with two bad penalties

E-Man had a normal snap count and had made them count. He picked up a sack, a pass defensed, nine tackles (with two TFLs), and even generated pressures while lined up as an edge rusher. I'm not pleased with the headbutt penalty (more on that later) but otherwise he was dominant against the Chargers offense.

Derius Davis muffed a punt, and O'Toole was there for the recovery (which led to a touchdown). While he's not part of the defensive rotation, he is a valuable special teams contributor when active on game days. I will not hold the helmet-to-helmet penalty against him because that was just bogus.

Stay on top of every Seahawks update and debate every snap with other members of the 12s. Game-day discussion is smoother in the SB Nation app.

Jump easily between conversations

Seattle has to clean its penalties up

As awful as Scott Novak's crew was, many of those Seahawks penalties were legit. The headbutt penalty by Nick Emmanwori on Cole Strange was a silly one to commit, especially given how flag-happy the refs were for other penalties earlier in the game. Emmanwori committed a face mask that extended a drive, Devon Witherspoon was flagged for unnecessary roughness, Derick Hall got a roughing the passer (which I didn't like, but I think is correct by the letter of the law) on 3rd and 24, it's all got to be fixed. Likewise for the pre-snap penalties like Jalen Sundell rocking in his stance before snapping the ball.

The Seahawks are one of the league's most penalized teams and they were their own worst enemy at the moment. When they run into a crew as flag-happy as Novak's, that is a cause for concern.

Brian Fleury needs to figure a couple of things out

Seattle's offensive coordinator has been put in a tough spot with injuries at key positions. The Seahawks third-down passing game is not consistent enough to threaten teams, and if Seattle is going to continue to get blitzed into oblivion then he needs to identify and find better blitz beaters. They're otherwise not equipped to come out on the positive side of obvious passing situations.

Additionally, too many drives are ending because of 2nd and long runs to nowhere, and he needs to figure out what plays are better run for Emanuel Wilson versus George Holani. The latter should never ever be the short-yardage option, and certainly not to the weaker side of the line.

On the plus side, Fleury has fixed the screen game which looked like an impossible task. That's a big plus for the first-year playcaller.

Enough of the Christian Haynes/Beau Stephens rotation

If Christian Haynes cannot be trusted to handle a full game of action then I don't know what to say. Your backup guard cannot be in a time-share deal because you want to give Beau Stephens rookie reps in non-garbage time situations. Haynes has been fine and to my recollection hasn't given up a pressure yet. Start Haynes until Anthony Bradford comes back. End of story. There was one series where Stephens got worked on multiple run plays, and I'm just exasperated that we're still doing this.

More special teams inconsistency

Jason Myers missed an extra point, missed a field goal (and was given a second life thanks to a Chargers penalty), and had another kickoff short of the landing zone. Coverage continues to be an issue on kickoffs, although at least they took advantage of Derius Davis' muffed punt. Something is not clicking with this ST unit on a consistent basis and it has to tighten up.

George Holani is a good "everything but running the ball" running back

I've harped on Holani a lot because John Schneider made glowing comments about him over the offseason after Kenneth Walker left. There was even some idle chatter among fans that George could get significant workload. Holani is ordinarily a very good pass-protecting back, a good special teams player who can return kicks, and a quality receiving back. When he actually has to run the ball he is so limited because he's not fast, doesn't break a lot of tackles, and can't push piles. Holani had 7 carries for 18 yards and now has 153 career rushing yards on 47 attempts. His longest carry to date is still 9 yards. These are fullback numbers.

When Zach Charbonnet comes back, it should be Emanuel Wilson and Charbonnet splitting the touches and Holani only in for the most situational snaps (third and obvious passing, maybe two-minute drills, etc.). Hopefully Zach is back sooner rather than later.

Not one, but two drops for Seattle's normally sure-handed tight ends. Three targets, one catch, two drops. Speaking of tight ends, which is up with Elijah Arroyo? Is he ever going to seriously get involved in this offense? Eric Saubert has more targets than he does!

Sam Darnold was nowhere near his best

The opening play interception was gross and inexplicable. Darnold sort of settled down the rest of the way and did throw a couple of touchdowns, but he was nearly picked again later in the game and seemed a bit fidgety in the pocket. No, he's not getting benched for Drew Lock like I saw suggested/recommended/considered. I guess after a one-year reprieve we're back to what's been almost a half-decade stretch of turnovers resulting in cries for the backup to play.

Something isn't quite clicking yet with Darnold on a per-down basis, so he's neither a Winner nor a Loser, but he's had a couple of iffy moments that are worth closer inspection over the next few weeks.

Is the run defense starting to crack just a tad?

Seattle's run defense has been exceptional for almost two full years under Coach Macdonald, but the Chargers had several successful run plays from their running backs. Kimani Vidal, Omarion Hampton, and Keaton Mitchell collectively had over 100 yards on 25 attempts, even if not one back broke out. The run defense is still great, but I am wondering if a better offense is poised to break the dam.

Byron Murphy II wrecked Trevor Penning for his first sack of the year. What a total mismatch that even sounds like on paper. That's Mike Tyson against Marvis Frazier levels of non-competitive.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba was "quiet." And by that, I mean he still led the team with five catches for 76 yards. There were plays in which he was open and Darnold either didn't see him or had pressure in his face and couldn't get to him in the progression.

Thankfully, Leonard Williams appears to be okay. That doesn't mean "play next week" okay but if it's not a long-term injury that's good news.

Scott Novak's crew needs to be far away from Seahawks games. Enough said.

The Seahawks need to clean things up or else they're in trouble over the next month. Home vs. 49ers, at Broncos on a short week, home vs. 4-0 Chiefs and 3-1 Bears (with Caleb Williams presumably back). From what I've seen through the first month, Seattle would do well to split these games. Denver actually looks like the most favorable game given the Broncos offense has struggled, but Seattle's offense has run hot and cold and the penalties in all three phases are a worry. Seattle hasn't played close to its best football yet, so if there was ever a time to do so, it's now.

title: The Sixers Roster Is A Math Problem Waiting To Explode
description: The 76ers have massive talent with Embiid, Maxey, and LeBron, but a massive usage rate overlap could lead to a repeat of the 2018 Celtics disaster.
fullText:
The Philadelphia 76ers are walking straight into a math trap. On paper, adding Jaylen Brown to a group featuring Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and LeBron James looks like a dream. In reality, the roster is so crowded with ball-dominant stars that a total collapse feels likely.

I have seen this movie before. It is a disaster waiting to happen, much like the 2018 Boston Celtics. Hardwood Houdini notes that the Celtics thought they were a sure thing back then. They believed they could win after adding stars like Kyrie Irving and Gordon Hayward. As the source puts it, "The Celtics just came within a game of the NBA Finals and are going to get Kyrie Irving and Gordon Hayward back? What could go wrong?" Everything went wrong.

The numbers for this Philly roster simply do not add up. You cannot have more than 100% of the ball in play. Yet, if you look at last season, the usage rates for these four players alone are staggering. According to Hardwood Houdini, the individual usage rates were:

That total reaches 126.3. That is a massive overshoot. When you add VJ Edgecombe at a 20.1 usage rate, the math gets even worse. You cannot find enough possessions to keep everyone happy.

The problem isn't a lack of talent. It is the lack of a "connector" role. We saw this in Boston. Jaylen Brown struggled because the team wanted him to play a role he could not handle. He ended up on the bench until Marcus Smart got hurt late in the season. The talent was there, but the fit was a wreck.

The Sixers are facing that same issue now. Embiid, Maxey, and LeBron are all players who need the ball to be effective. They are not role players. They are used to being the center of the offense. If they cannot play off the ball, the whole system breaks. The 76ers have all the pieces for a special team, but they might just end up with a very expensive trainwreck.

title: Golden State Valkyries flex their depth to expose Aces’ flaws in Game 1 of WNBA semifinals
